title: Migrate @earendil-works/pi-server -> @oh-my-pi/pi-server by verbatim copy; LAST of the 7, blocked on chord + pi-protocol, and on one type omp does not have
one_line: pi-server is a transport-neutral, length-framed CBOR RPC server that hosts durable Sessions over a Unix-domain-socket listener and routes contract-agnostic chord service calls per presentation attachment — 16 source files / 67,005 bytes, and the only one of the seven new packages with ZERO external npm dependencies of its own (its sole dep `esbuild` belongs to chord, and its other two deps are the sibling packages chord and pi-protocol).
why_copy_not_reimplement:
Three reasons, each tied to a contract a rewrite would silently lose.

(1) The state machine is the product. `Server` is 576 lines whose value is almost entirely in ORDERING, not in any algorithm: `awaitingHello → handshaking → ready → closing → closed`; a handshake whose `finishHandshake` promise has not settled must QUEUE subsequent messages rather than drop them (server.ts:252-259); a `hello` that arrives after the handshake is refused while one that arrives during it is awaited; and a request that fails AFTER it already responded must close the connection instead of sending a second response (server.ts:387-390). A reimplementation reproduces none of this for free — it reproduces it only if someone has read all 576 lines and understood why each branch exists. 5 of the 39 upstream tests exist purely to pin this ordering (`requires hello as the first message`, `accepts fragmented hello and request frames`, `rejects a second hello after completing the handshake`, `processes a hello and request coalesced in one byte chunk`, `reports a truncated final frame when the peer closes`). Copying carries the ordering and its tests together; a rewrite has to re-derive both and then prove the re-derivation.

(2) The failure handling is the contract, and it is unguessable. Every cleanup path in this package is an AggregateError with a specific argument list and a specific report-vs-throw decision: `startInternal` closes already-started listeners before rethrowing and wraps the original error with every cleanup error (server.ts:124-128); `closeInternal` collapses a single failure to that error and multiple failures to `new AggregateError(errors, "Server shutdown failed")` (server.ts:197-203); `handleRequest` deletes the subscription encoder only when it installed one and had not yet responded (server.ts:384-386); `removeSession` throws one error bare but aggregates many, and does so with the message `Failed to close Session ${sessionId}` (session-router.ts:87-88). A rewrite gets all of this subtly wrong in ways that only surface when a listener fails to close during shutdown — the exact scenario `test/server.test.ts:111` ("rejects close and closed when listener shutdown fails") and `test/conformance.test.ts:479` ("fails shutdown when an in-flight acquisition cannot release its Harness") exist to catch. These are 5 lines each, and they are the lines you cannot reconstruct from the interface.

(3) The filesystem-safety logic in the Unix listener is genuinely subtle and load-bearing. `removeStaleSocket` refuses to unlink a non-socket, refuses when a live listener answers a connect probe, renames the target to a sibling, RE-STATs it, and restores the original name if the inode changed underneath it; `cleanupOwnedSocket` does the same dance in reverse to avoid deleting a replacement. `start` binds a private `bind-<sha256-prefix>` path, `link()`s it to the public name, `chmod`s, then unlinks the private one — so a crashed startup never publishes a half-configured socket. That is ~90 lines of TOCTOU-aware code in a 421-line file, and a regression in it deletes a user's regular file. `test/unix.test.ts` has 5 cases devoted to it, including "never unlinks a regular file at the configured path" and "does not remove a replacement inode during shutdown". Reimplementing this is the single highest-risk thing in the whole wave, and copying it is free.

Bonus, and it is what makes the mechanical pass so cheap: this package imports NOTHING from the npm ecosystem. Its dependencies are `@earendil-works/chord`, `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core`, `@earendil-works/pi-protocol` — all in-wave siblings — and its devDependencies (`shx`, `vitest`) are both droppable. No `esbuild`, no `typebox`, no third-party runtime surface enters through this door. Copy-then-migrate costs 38 scope substitutions and 57 `.ts`-suffix strips; a hand-port would cost the same design work with none of the provenance and none of the MIT notice trail that makes future upstream merges possible.

new_dependencies.name: @oh-my-pi/chord
new_dependencies.why: Hard dep. pi-server imports 11 chord symbols across 7 files: types JsonValue/ServiceCall/ServiceProviderUpdate/ServiceStateEncoder/RemoteServiceErrorCode, values createServiceStateEncoder/decodeServiceControlCall/parseServiceCall/parseServiceSubscriptionSnapshot/RemoteServiceError. Server cannot typecheck without it.
new_dependencies.license: MIT (Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner) — same notice as the root LICENSE already carries.

new_dependencies.name: @oh-my-pi/pi-protocol
new_dependencies.why: Hard dep, and the harder of the two. 18 symbols across 6 files: ClientMessageDecoder, encodeServerMessage, encodeClientMessage, ServerMessageDecoder, encodeFrame, encodeCbor, DEFAULT_MAX_FRAME_LENGTH, PROTOCOL_VERSION, isServerId, isSupportedProtocolVersion, ProtocolValidationError + 8 envelope types. Its own upstream dep is `typebox@1.3.27`; omp has only `@sinclair/typebox@0.34.52` (transitive) and an unrelated `@oh-my-pi/omptype`. typebox is NOT in the omp catalog, so pi-protocol's spec must decide it before server can land.

new_dependencies.name: @oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core
new_dependencies.why: Declared dep, but only ONE of its five imported symbols actually has to come from there: SessionMetadata. The other four (Context, BACKGROUND_CONTEXT, TODO_CONTEXT, withAbortSignal) are pure re-exports of `@earendil-works/chord/context` in upstream pi — see pi's packages/agent/src/harness/context.ts:14-25, which re-exports all of them from chord. Repoint those four at `@oh-my-pi/chord/context` and the package stops depending on agent-core except for SessionMetadata. See collisions[2].

collisions.what: The `Server` class name. pi-server exports `class Server<TMetadata>`. omp uses the bare word `Server` for two unrelated things: packages/metaharness/src/server.ts:26 does `import type { Server, Subprocess } from "bun"` and annotates `#server: Server<undefined> | null` (line 194), and packages/stats/src/server.ts is a whole file of the same name.
collisions.pi_anchor: packages/server/src/server.ts:46 — `export class Server<TMetadata extends SessionMetadata = SessionMetadata>`
collisions.omp_anchor: packages/metaharness/src/server.ts:26,194 (`import type { Server } from "bun"`; `#server: Server<undefined> | null`) and packages/stats/src/server.ts
collisions.resolution: KEEP BOTH — no edit to either. They are different packages with different module specifiers, so no import can ever be ambiguous: `@oh-my-pi/pi-server`'s `Server` only enters scope via `import { Server } from "@oh-my-pi/pi-server"`, which never collides with a local `import type { Server } from "bun"` in a different module. The only real hazard is a FUTURE file that imports both; if that happens, alias the Bun one as `BunServer` at the import site rather than renaming the migrated class. Do not rename the migrated class — upstream name fidelity is the whole point of a copy-based migration.

collisions.what: `MaybePromise<T> = T | Promise<T>` declared twice. pi-server declares and star-exports its own at types.ts:15. omp already has a byte-identical declaration in a shared package.
collisions.pi_anchor: packages/server/src/types.ts:15 — `export type MaybePromise<T> = T | Promise<T>;` (re-exported by src/index.ts:4)
collisions.omp_anchor: packages/utils/src/acp/protocol.ts:9 — `export type MaybePromise<T> = T | Promise<T>;` (reachable as `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/acp/protocol` via the `./*` export wildcard)
collisions.resolution: DROP the local declaration; add `export type { MaybePromise } from "@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/acp/protocol";` to src/types.ts so the public API of pi-server is byte-identical but the type has exactly one home. AGENTS.md 'Central Utilities' is explicit that a second implementation of an existing helper is a bug. This is the ONE intentional non-verbatim edit to a public symbol, and it is type-only, so it cannot change runtime behavior.

collisions.what: `SessionMetadata` — the generic bound on ServerHost/Server/SessionRouter/createUnixServer — does not exist anywhere in omp, and omp's `@oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core` is NOT the same package as pi's despite the identical name.
collisions.pi_anchor: packages/server/src/types.ts:59 `ServerHost<TMetadata extends SessionMetadata = SessionMetadata>`; the type itself is pi's packages/agent/src/harness/session/types.ts:473 — a 6-field interface: `{ id: string; createdAt: number; storageVersion: number; cwd?: string; parentSessionId?: string; legacyParentSessionPath?: string }`
collisions.omp_anchor: packages/agent/src/index.ts exports only 18 flat modules (agent, agent-loop, append-only-context, compaction, output-budget, pause, proxy, replay-policy, run-collector, sent-tool-definitions, speculative-execution, telemetry, thinking, tool-context, tokenizer, types, utils/yield). `grep -rn 'SessionMetadata' packages/agent/src` returns 0 hits. The entire `harness/` subtree is absent: omp pi-agent-core is 34 files / 739,550 bytes vs pi's 117 files / 1,145,928 bytes. omp also has no `MemorySessionRepo`, no `Session` interface, no `SessionReader`, no `SessionDirectory` (all measured 0 across packages/).
collisions.resolution: DECLARE IT LOCALLY in pi-server. Add the 6-field `SessionMetadata` interface verbatim to packages/server/src/types.ts and import it from there instead of from pi-agent-core, then delete the 7 pi-agent-core import lines. Rationale: (a) the other four agent-core symbols (Context, BACKGROUND_CONTEXT, TODO_CONTEXT, withAbortSignal) are re-exports of chord/context upstream, so repointing them to `@oh-my-pi/chord/context` leaves SessionMetadata as the ONLY residue; (b) omp has no durable-Session concept at all, so there is nothing in-tree for this type to alias to; (c) declaring it here makes pi-server landable as a standalone package instead of hostage to a much larger agent-core reconciliation that is out of scope for this spec. This is a deliberate, named deviation from verbatim — see open_questions[0] for the owner's call.

collisions.what: `TestServerHost` depends on `MemorySessionRepo`, a pi-agent-core session-repository abstraction with no omp counterpart and no obvious home.
collisions.pi_anchor: packages/server/src/testing/host.ts:3 `import { BACKGROUND_CONTEXT, MemorySessionRepo } from "@earendil-works/pi-agent-core";` and :153 `readonly repo = new MemorySessionRepo({ now: () => 1 });` — used by resolveSession (list), openSession (open), and seed (create)
collisions.omp_anchor: none — `grep -rn 'MemorySessionRepo' packages/` returns 0 hits. omp's closest analogue is packages/coding-agent/src/session/, which is a single-process session manager with no repository interface.
collisions.resolution: REPLACE with a ~30-line in-file `TestSessionRepo` in src/testing/host.ts: keep a `Map<string, SessionMetadata>` plus an in-memory `Session` shim, and give it the three methods the harness calls (list/open/create) so the observable contract the conformance tests assert — resolveSession returns 0 matches → SessionNotFoundError, >1 → SessionAmbiguousError, exactly 1 → that metadata — is unchanged. Do NOT try to introduce a real session-repository abstraction here; that is pi-durable's job and it is a separate package in the wave.

collisions.what: Role overlap with the two packages the brief flagged. Neither is a functional duplicate, but both would be mistaken for one by a reader.
collisions.pi_anchor: packages/server/src/server.ts:136 `accept(connection: ByteConnection): ByteConnectionHandler` — accepts an already-authorized ordered byte stream. Zero HTTP, zero WebSocket, zero MCP anywhere in the package (verified: the only node:net import is transports/unix/listener.ts:4).
collisions.omp_anchor: packages/collab-web/src/lib/socket.ts (browser WebSocket to a relay room, AES-GCM sealed frames via codec.ts, 4-digit close codes 4001/4004/4009/4029 in RELAY_CLOSE_REASONS) and packages/collab-web/src/lib/link.ts (`wss://host/r/<roomId>.<base64url-key>`) vs packages/metaharness/src/server.ts:211 `Bun.serve({ port, routes, fetch })` — REST + SSE over HTTP for the benchmark run store.
collisions.resolution: NO MERGE, and record the distinction in the new packages/server/README.md so the next reader does not re-litigate it. pi-server is: length-framed CBOR (pi-protocol) over a Unix socket, a hello/hello_error handshake with PROTOCOL_VERSION = 8, request/response/cancel plus out-of-band attachment and service_update messages, and per-attachment service routing. collab-web is: a WebSocket relay with browser-safe crypto, room-scoped, no handshake version gate. metaharness is: an HTTP/SSE process manager. Three different transports, three different auth models, three different lifecycles. The genuine adjacent art in omp is packages/coding-agent/src/collab/registry.ts (762 lines) and src/tiny/jsonl-socket.ts (49 lines) — both node:net + Unix-socket hosts, but newline-delimited JSON rather than length-framed CBOR, so they remain the idiomatic in-tree pattern for their own protocols and must NOT be refactored onto pi-server.

test_contract:
Seven test files, 39 cases, all rewritten to `bun:test`, all contract-level. None is a static echo, none is a success passthrough, none reads an implementation file's text, and none uses `mock.module()` (which AGENTS.md bans outright because Bun's module-registry mutation leaks across files).

WHAT EACH FILE PROVES, and the failure a consumer observes if each regresses:

- `test/conformance.test.ts` (502 lines, 20 cases, 2 describes) — the attachment-routing contract. A client that attaches to a Session, routes a service call, and loses the connection must observe: the attachment released only after admitted calls settle (a session is never closed while a service call is in flight); a request from a connection that does NOT hold the targeted {sessionId, attachmentId} is rejected with `session_not_attached`; a stale attachmentId after switching Sessions is rejected; a request addressed to a different serverId is rejected BEFORE any repository lookup; an unknown session raises `session_not_found` without constructing a Harness; an ambiguous sessionId raises `session_ambiguous` without constructing a Harness; a terminated Harness handle is evicted and a later attach succeeds; server shutdown closes every routed handle. These are the guarantees a remote-presentation client depends on — a regression here means a guest either loses its session or talks to a dead one.

- `test/protocol.test.ts` (168 lines, 5 cases) — the framing/handshake contract on a pure in-memory `ByteConnection` (no sockets, no ports, no timers, fully deterministic). hello must be the first message; an unsupported PROTOCOL_VERSION is refused; a frame split across two `onData` calls decodes identically; a second hello is refused; a hello and a request coalesced in ONE byte chunk both process in order; a truncated final frame is surfaced as an error when the peer closes. Observable effect: a client on a slow or lossy link must never see a half-parsed session.

- `test/server.test.ts` (127 lines, 6 cases) — the options and lifecycle contract. A non-UUIDv4 serverId and a missing listeners array are rejected with TypeError; maxFrameLength/handshakeTimeoutMs out of range are rejected (including above Node's 2_147_483_647 ms timer ceiling); a second concurrent `start()` is refused without leaking the already-started listener; a handshake that never arrives is closed with a FINAL `hello_error` frame in the last write; `close()` propagates a listener-shutdown failure instead of resolving. Observable effect: a misconfigured launcher fails at boot rather than serving a broken server.

- `test/listener.test.ts` (52 lines, 2 cases) — the composition contract. Every configured listener starts; if listener N fails, listeners 1..N-1 are closed. Observable effect: a partial-transport server never runs with half its transports up.

- `test/unix.test.ts` (143 lines, 5 cases) — the filesystem-safety contract on real temp-dir sockets. A live listener at the target path is REFUSED, not unlinked; a regular file at the path is never unlinked; a nested parent dir is created 0o700 and the socket left 0o600 and removed on close; a replacement inode appearing during shutdown is NOT removed; a genuinely stale socket IS removed before binding. This is the sharpest test set in the package: a regression means the server deletes a user's file. It uses real `node:net` sockets and the `fixtures/stale-socket-server.mjs` child process.

- `test/unix-connection.test.ts` (65 lines, 1 case) — the backpressure/close-ordering contract: a final protocol-error frame is queued BEHIND pending output rather than racing it, so a client always reads the error before EOF.

- `test/fixtures/stale-socket-server.mjs` (9 lines) — not a test; a `node:net` listener that binds a path and never accepts, used by the stale-socket case.

MIGRATION-SIDE TEST CHANGES REQUIRED: `vitest` -> `bun:test` in all 7; the two `BackgroundContext`/`SessionMetadata` imports in conformance.test.ts repointed; `.ts` suffixes stripped from 24 relative specifiers across the 6 `.ts` test files. Every `expect` matcher used upstream (`toBe`, `toMatchObject`, `rejects.toThrow`, `resolves`, `toEqual`) exists in `bun:test`; upstream uses no `vi.*` timer or module API, so no behavioural test surgery is needed — only the import line changes. After the rewrite, the contract above is UNCHANGED: the same 39 assertions, same names, same observable guarantees.

The mechanical part is trivial: 29 files / 115,351 bytes total, of which only 16 files / 67,005 bytes are source, and the scope+`.ts`-suffix pass is 38 + 57 string substitutions that a script does in under a second. The cost is entirely in the four non-mechanical sweeps and one blocking dependency question:

- step 6 (`private` -> `#private`): 20 fields across 3 files, mechanical but touch-heavy (~40 call sites including the `get closed()` accessor).
- step 7 (Promise.withResolvers + `NodeJS.Timeout` -> `Timer`): 5 of 6 promise sites, plus 4 timer type positions.

risk:
HIGH, and for a reason that is easy to miss: this package is the LAST of the seven and it is the only one whose stated premise does not hold.

The brief's measured fact — "omp already has `pi-agent-core` and `pi-ai` under the same names, only the scope differs" — is true of the NAMES and false of the PACKAGES. omp's `packages/agent` is 34 files / 739,550 bytes exporting 18 flat modules; pi's is 117 files / 1,145,928 bytes with an entire `harness/` subtree. `grep -rn 'SessionMetadata' packages/agent/src` returns 0. omp has no `Context`, no `Session`, no `MemorySessionRepo`, no `SessionReader`, no `SessionDirectory` — all measured 0 across every package. So `ServerHost<TMetadata extends SessionMetadata>` has nothing in omp to bind to, and the seven pi-agent-core import lines cannot be rewritten by scope substitution; they are the package's real integration surface.

That said, the exposure is narrower than it looks, and that is the load-bearing finding of this spec: of the five symbols pi-server imports from pi-agent-core, FOUR (`Context`, `BACKGROUND_CONTEXT`, `TODO_CONTEXT`, `withAbortSignal`) are not agent-core concepts at all — pi's own `packages/agent/src/harness/context.ts:14-25` re-exports them verbatim from `@earendil-works/chord/context`. Once chord lands, they come from `@oh-my-pi/chord/context` and the agent-core dependency effectively evaporates. What remains is ONE type: `SessionMetadata`, a 6-field interface. That is the whole gap, and it is small enough to close inside this package (collisions[2]) without waiting on, or dictating, an agent-core reconciliation that is far out of scope.

Second risk, and the one most likely to actually break the build: the `typebox` wall. pi-protocol declares `typebox@1.3.27` and builds every envelope type with `Static<typeof XSchema>` / `Type.Union`. omp's lockfile has only the unrelated `@sinclair/typebox@0.34.52` (transitive) plus `@oh-my-pi/omptype`, which is an ArkType-compatible validator, not a typebox. pi-protocol is NOT in the omp catalog. Server cannot typecheck until pi-protocol lands, and pi-protocol may need a schema-library decision of its own. This is a chain, not a detail: pi-server is blocked behind a decision that belongs to a different package's spec.

Third risk, lower but real: `session-router.ts` and `server.ts` are the two files where a subtle rewrite turns a correct concurrency contract into a subtly wrong one. SessionRouter serializes every operation per client through `runForClient`, keeps three separate Maps plus a `disconnectedClients` Set, and distinguishes "release after admitted calls settle" from "release immediately." The 20 conformance cases are the only thing standing between a refactor and a session-close race, and they cannot run until ninja is installed. Do not let the vitest->bun:test conversion be treated as mechanical until GATE 2 has actually executed 39 green cases.

Fourth, and cheapest to state: `chord` drags in `esbuild@0.28.2`, absent from omp. That is chord's spec to solve, not this one's, but it is on the critical path and belongs in the milestone plan.

Not a risk: the collision with `collab-web` and `metaharness`. Measured, not assumed — pi-server is length-framed CBOR over Unix sockets with a versioned handshake; collab-web is WebSocket + AES-GCM room relay; metaharness is `Bun.serve` REST+SSE. Three transports, three auth models. The real adjacent art is `packages/coding-agent/src/collab/registry.ts` (762 lines of node:net + newline-JSON Unix-socket host), which must NOT be refactored onto pi-server, and the spec says so explicitly so the question is closed rather than re-litigated later.
